newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt in talks on seismic work for remote areas.
newsitem.headline: Egypt in talks on seismic work for remote areas.

text.p: The state Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) said on Wednesday it was negotiating with the U.S. companies Western Atlas and Wavetech Inc on non-exclusive surveys of three large oil exploration blocks.
Sami Shahin, EGPC vice-president for concessions, told Reuters on Wednesday that the companies would have the right to market the surveys, sharing part of the profits with EGPC.
If EGPC reaches agreements with the companies, the three blocks will be withdrawn from this year's bid round and offered to oil companies later, perhaps next year, he said.
The three areas are West Mediterranean Deep Water A, West Mediterranean Deep Water B and North El Mesaha Trough.

The first two, totalling 37,200 square km (14,400 square miles), are in deep water off the northwestern coast. El Mesaha is an area of 62,987 square km (24,313 square miles) touching the Sudanese border towards the southwestern corner of Egypt.
"We are negotiating a seismic survey for the first two and both aeromagnetic and seismic for El Mesaha," Shahin said.
"This is because they are frontier areas and have hardly been explored at all. We are not interested in making money, just in making the data available," he said.
Shahin also gave details of the seven oil exploration blocks which EGPC has added to those on offer in the 1997 bid round, making a total of 15. These are:

- North Idku, 988 square km straddling the coastline near the Nile Delta town of Abu Qir. The commercial gas fields at Abu Qir, operated by Phillips Petroleum and EGPC, have been extracted from the concession.

- Qantara, 150 square km on the western bank of the Suez Canal. Shahin said International Egyptian Oil Company (IEOC), the Egyptian affiliate of Agip, had relinquished the area and USX Marathon had asked for it because it lies in the middle of another Marathon concession.
- El Mansoura, 1,840 square km around the Nile Delta town of Mansoura and surrounding the commercial Abu Madi gas fields operated by IEOC and EGPC.

- North West Damietta, 901 square km offshore from the Nile Delta town of Damietta, relinquished by Amoco in 1996 and formerly known as East Baltim. It lies just north of the Qara field and just east of the Baltim field and is likely to attract much interest from oil companies.

- North El Arish, 2,120 square km offshore from the North Sinai town of el-Arish, up to the border with Gaza. This is a partial relinquishment by British Gas. Oil companies have reported oil and gas shows in the area but none of them have reached commercial development.
- North Rahmi, 196 square km offshore in the Gulf of Suez, also a partial relinquishment by British Gas.
- West Belayim, 209 square km also offshore in the Gulf of Suez. Companies have drilled seven wells there over the years.

Shahin said that the Assiut block, listed earlier as part of the 1997 bid round, should not be on the list. The eighth block on the original list is in fact Western Gharib, 2,530 square km on the western shores of the Gulf of Suez.
